title: Stellar masses and disk properties of Lupus young stellar objects traced by velocity-aligned stacked ALMA <SUP>13</SUP>CO and C<SUP>18</SUP>O spectra
question: Can velocity-aligned stacking of 13CO and C18O (3-2) data from the ALMA Lupus survey yield more detections, dynamical stellar masses, disk orientations and gas masses, and how do gas masses relate to dust masses and accretion rates?

data.bands: 0.9 mm continuum (Band 7), simultaneous with 13CO and C18O (3-2)
data.sensitivity: 70 and 67 mJy/beam per channel for 13CO and C18O

what.value: Spectroscopic stellar masses and mass accretion rates

evidence.quote: $M_{\star,{\rm spec}}$ is the spectroscopically determined stellar mass from (cite: Alcala14; Alcala17).

what.value: Continuum fluxes, source coordinates, continuum PA and inclinations

evidence.quote: The coordinates are obtained from (cite: Ansdell16).

what.value: Grids of physical-chemical disk models for gas mass

evidence.loc: Measured Stellar Mass and Disk Properties
evidence.quote: our measurements and the expected $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O line luminosities of protoplanetary disks with different masses from models by (cite: Williams14) and (cite: Miotello16).

recipe.method: Calibrate with standard cycle-2 script and clean with Briggs weighting

recipe.goal: Grid search with velocity-aligned stacking for M*, PA, i, Vsys
recipe.method: Shift spectra by projected Keplerian velocities, integrate within 1 arcsec de-projected radius, maximize S/N of Gaussian-weighted integrated intensity; uncertainties from parameter ranges giving consistent line profiles
key_parameters: detection: peak >4 sigma and >=3 channels above 3 sigma within 2 sigma Gaussian width
assumptions: geometrically thin Keplerian disk; stellar position at continuum center; distances 150/200 pc

recipe.method: Apply best parameters; stack in radial bins (half-beam steps) to find detected radius (2 sigma); integrate within twice the FWHM line width; apply same to C18O
key_parameters: C18O detection above 4 sigma; 20% systematic flux uncertainty
assumptions: 13CO and C18O trace the same regions

recipe.method: Compare 13CO and C18O luminosities with Williams & Best 2014 and Miotello+16 grids (luminosity-weighted mean mass); Miotello+17 fitting function for 13CO-only disks
key_parameters: face-on vs edge-on fit function split at i=70 deg
assumptions: No volatile carbon depletion in the models

recipe.method: Bayesian linear fit in log space with errors on both axes, using log of upper limit/measurement as 1 sigma
key_parameters: disks with dust mass <1e-6 Msun excluded

evidence.quote: We obtain $^{13}$CO detections in 41 disks and C$^{18}$O detections in 18 disks

answer_key.quantity: Mean dynamical vs spectroscopic mass difference (16 sources)

evidence.quote: The mean difference between the dynamical and spectroscopic stellar masses in this subsample is 0.15 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Slope of log gas vs log dust mass

evidence.quote: with a slope of 1.1$\pm$0.5 and a correlation coefficient of 0.8$\pm$0.2
measured the standard deviation of the residual gas masses to be 0.9 dex
is relatively flat and has a median of 12

answer_key.quantity: Mean inclination difference vs continuum (23 disks)

evidence.loc: Measured Stellar Mass and Disk Properties
evidence.quote: The mean difference of the disk inclination, $i$, measured from our method and from the continuum emission is 15$^\circ$

not_stated_but_needed: Code for the stacking/alignment and S/N search (not released)
Exact clean parameters (image size, cell, threshold, masks)
Exact outlier-trimming rule for S/N distribution
Model-grid details for the luminosity-weighted gas mass averaging
Dust mass conversion details (taken from Ansdell16/Miotello17)
score_reason: Public data and a clear algorithm with parameter grids, but code and some imaging and conversion details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data and a clearly described method with numeric results, though code is needed to be rewritten.
